Witness:
$$
M = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}
$$

Verification:
The matrix $ M $ has entries in $[0,1]$, is not stochastic because its second row sums to 0, not 1. The kernel of $(M - I)^T$ is computed as follows:

$$
M - I = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix}, \quad (M - I)^T = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 \end{pmatrix}
$$

The kernel of $(M - I)^T$ consists of vectors $ \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} $ such that:

$$
\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}
$$

This gives the equation $ y - x = 0 $, or $ y = x $. So the kernel is all vectors of the form $ \begin{pmatrix} x \\ x \end{pmatrix} $, which are nonpositive if and only if $ x \leq 0 $. Thus, the kernel contains only nonpositive vectors.
